item.title: Putin releases American Stephen Hubbard from Russian prison
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has freed another American, 74-year-old Michigan native Stephen Hubbard, from a Russian prison following a request from President Trump.

item.title: Meet the people moving north to escape increasingly hot summers
item.description: As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?
item.content:encoded:
As climate change fuels hotter summers, some Britons are moving north in search of cooler weather. Could a similar shift be on the horizon in the United States?

(Image credit: Dan Kitwood)

item.title: Israel frees dozens of Americans, including U.S. Congress nominee, after West Bank detention
item.description: Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander along with dozens of American and Israeli rabbis and activists were helping Palestinian olive harvesters when they were detained by Israeli forces.

item.title: DOJ's noncitizen voter list is unreliable, officials say. And, U.S. pollution rises
item.description: The Justice Department's "likely" noncitizen voter list in California is "unreliable," according to officials. And, the United Nations reports a major increase in U.S. climate pollution.

item.title: Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine on Trump's turn toward Russia
item.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep asks former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst about President Trump's embrace of Russia as envoy Steve Witkoff heads to Moscow after meeting Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

item.title: Russia releases imprisoned U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard following Trump's request
item.description: The announcement of Hubbard's release came as talks got underway between Putin and White House envoy Steve Witkoff in Saint Petersburg focused on the latest U.S. efforts to end the war in Ukraine.

item.title: France announces nightly curfews 'for as long as necessary' in Paris and other cities
item.description: Fresh curfews were being imposed across the city centers of Paris and Lyon on Tuesday after the first quiet night since France's most destructive rioting in years.
